items.text: AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time (an execution is protected from being superseded once it is actually running in a stage).

In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a newer execution can supersede an execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, so the waiting execution is dropped and never runs (a queued deployment can be silently skipped).
The linked AWS docs page https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/concepts-how-it-works.html exists and documents CodePipeline execution modes.
`QUEUED` is a valid AWS CodePipeline execution mode.
In CodePipeline's `QUEUED` execution mode, waiting executions form a queue and each runs in turn; a later execution does not supersede/drop an earlier waiting one.
The CodePipeline `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline (pipeline type V2), so `pipelineType` must be set along with `executionMode`.
The AWS CLI's CodePipeline `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands can set a pipeline's execution mode and pipeline type.
The Pulumi AWS provider's `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource has an `executionMode` input (source: pulumi/pulumi-aws).
The Pulumi AWS provider's `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource has a `pipelineType` input (source: pulumi/pulumi-aws).
The registry page /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/ exists (target of the `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` link).
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource is described below on the aws-code-services page (in the 'Manage the pipeline with Pulumi' section).
When two runs attempt to update the same Pulumi stack at the same time, Pulumi Cloud grants the stack lease to only one of them.
When two concurrent runs target the same stack, the run that does not get the Pulumi Cloud lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update-conflict error.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists (target of the 'update conflict' link).

Azure Pipelines supports an 'exclusive lock' check that can be applied to an environment, which prevents concurrent runs of deployment jobs targeting that environment (source: learn.microsoft.com approvals/checks docs).
The linked Microsoft page https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/devops/pipelines/process/approvals?view=azure-devops exists and documents the exclusive lock check.
In Azure DevOps, the exclusive lock check is added from an environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
Azure Pipelines YAML supports a stage-level `lockBehavior` property that controls how a stage acquires an exclusive lock on the environment it references.
The default value of Azure Pipelines' `lockBehavior` is `runLatest`.
`sequential` is a valid value for Azure Pipelines' stage `lockBehavior` property.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock; an older run waiting behind it is passed over (cancelled) rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage acquires the exclusive lock in order, one at a time, so no queued run is skipped.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack, running them one at a time.
The Pulumi Azure DevOps provider has an `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource for managing an exclusive lock check as code (source: pulumi/pulumi-azuredevops).
The registry page /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/ exists (target of the `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` link).
When two builds attempt to update the same Pulumi stack at the same time, Pulumi Cloud grants the stack lease to only one of them.
When two concurrent builds target the same stack, the build that does not get the Pulumi Cloud lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update-conflict error.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists (target of the 'update conflict' link).
By default, TeamCity lets builds of the same build configuration run concurrently on as many free agents as are available (no limit on simultaneous builds).
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds'.
The TeamCity 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' option is found under the build configuration's General Settings (as an advanced option).
The default value of TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' option is `0`, which means unlimited.
Setting TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to `1` causes a second build of that configuration to be queued behind the first and run only after the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud uses a per-stack lease that allows only one update to a stack at a time (one-at-a-time behavior).
The anchor /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/#serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock exists on the Azure DevOps guide.

In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment a deployment job targets, together with `lockBehavior: sequential` on the stage, prevents concurrent deployments to the same stack (they are serialized).
The anchor /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/#serialize-pipeline-executions exists on the AWS Code Services guide.
Setting an AWS CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn rather than being superseded.
AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode lets a newer execution supersede an older execution that is still waiting to start.
The anchor /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/#limit-concurrent-builds exists on the TeamCity guide.
Setting TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' option to `1` on a build configuration prevents concurrent deployment builds of that configuration (serializes them).
